headline: I regret choosing an effigy-burning as the venue for my daughter’s protest-themed wedding
body:
I had high hopes for a thematic ceremony, thinking that a fiery protest backdrop would be the ultimate aesthetic for our social justice-themed nuptials in Ranchi. When I hired a local decorator to craft papier-mâché replicas of the state’s top leaders, I specifically requested 'biodegradable, slow-burning, and socially conscious.' Unfortunately, the local protest group down the street decided to hijack my centerpiece for their own scuffle with the police, and my daughter’s wedding march was quickly drowned out by chanting and the smell of melting synthetic hair.

Everything went sideways the moment the effigy of the Chief Minister started listing to the left while being wrestled away by a constable who seemed to take the whole thing very personally. My florist spent most of the afternoon trying to recover the marigold garlands from the middle of a police barricade, while my mother-in-law insisted that the sudden shouting match was just a very intense, authentic version of our traditional pre-wedding banter.

Now I am left with a half-burnt effigy of a prominent political figure in my garden, a wedding videographer who claims he can’t 'edit out the baton charges' without charging an extra service fee, and a very confused catering staff who still don't know if the protest was technically part of the buffet itinerary. I suppose if nothing else, the guests certainly won't be forgetting the seating arrangements anytime soon.
caption: When the protest is literally on your wedding invite list. #Ranchi #WeddingDrama #ProtestSeason #EffigyLife (satire)
